title: Knowledge check: Profiling and Measuring Performance

questions.prompt: Which approach best matches “Profiling and Measuring Performance”?
options: Render every row in a huge list even if only a small window is visible.
Choose an optimization without measuring current behavior.
Measure a reproducible baseline, profile the constrained resource, and compare the same scenario after a change.
questions.answer_key: Measure a reproducible baseline, profile the constrained resource, and compare the same scenario after a change.
questions.explanation: This answer addresses Profiling and Measuring Performance directly. Verify the behavior in a small Vue 3 example and check the runtime requirements in the linked official reference.

questions.prompt: For “Vue DevTools profiling”, which practice is most reliable?
options: Choose an optimization without measuring current behavior.
Measure a reproducible baseline, profile the constrained resource, and compare the same scenario after a change.
Render every row in a huge list even if only a small window is visible.
questions.answer_key: Measure a reproducible baseline, profile the constrained resource, and compare the same scenario after a change.
questions.explanation: This practice supports the syllabus subtopic “Vue DevTools profiling”. Check the expected result and a relevant boundary or failure case.

questions.prompt: A learner example for “Profiling and Measuring Performance” behaves unexpectedly. What should be checked first?
options: Reproduce the state or input change, inspect the relevant Vue binding or dependency, and compare the result with the expected output.
Change unrelated files until the page looks correct.
Disable error handling and assume the framework is at fault.
Trust a client-supplied success flag without checking behavior.
questions.answer_key: Reproduce the state or input change, inspect the relevant Vue binding or dependency, and compare the result with the expected output.
questions.explanation: Start with a small reproducible case. Inspect the element, reactive source, Console, and expected result before changing unrelated code.

review_note: Answer keys and explanations are server-side data. Human review required before publication.
